title: Horror 3D
description: A first-person horror game in the style of Slender: collect the pages scattered through a dark forest before the thing hunting you catches up. Pawel Jarosz's entry to Made With Defold Jam 2023.
author: Pawel Jarosz
controls: WASD or the left stick (or d-pad) move, the mouse or the right stick look, Shift or LT run, Space or A jump, C or B crouch, F or Y flashlight, E or X collects a page, H or START hides the UI, N or SELECT toggles the scare jumps, 1/2 or LB/RB adjust brightness.
credits: Based on Illumination by Roman Silin (astrochili), MIT, and Horri-fold post-processing by Aayush Kashyap (TheKing0x9).
Models from cgtrader free models: low-poly zombie, dead trees, realistic trees pack, metal door, cross stone, candles set, meatcube arm; each is credited by link in the project README.
Depends on defold-operator and defold-trenchbroom (Roman Silin), pigeon (Pawel Jarosz) and defold-pointer-lock (Indiesoft LLC).
notes: pointer_lock (indiesoftby/defold-pointer-lock) is replaced by cart-ext/pointer_lock: the original locks the cursor through GLFW or the browser, neither of which a cart has. Its Lua half is unchanged.

GL ES precision: game.project sets [shader] glsl_es_default_precision_float = highp. Defold defaults GL ES fragment shaders to mediump, and drivers that honour it (Mesa here, mobile GPUs) build the Illumination normal-map tangent frame from 16-bit view-direction derivatives: it comes out infinite and every light vanishes. Desktop GL and WebGPU always ran it at full precision.

Gamepad (added for the cart; upstream is keyboard and mouse): walker.script reads the left stick, d-pad, A, B, LT and L3 as the keys they stand for; player.script turns the right stick into the operator's manual_control look (no pointer lock; a 0.12 dead zone, 160 and 110 degrees a second at full deflection, a 1.6 response curve) and puts the flashlight on Y; hint.gui_script puts collect on X, hide UI on START, the scare toggle on SELECT and brightness on LB/RB. The on-screen hints name both.

Pages are in reach by distance (scene.script, 1.4 m), not by the player's interact trigger: on this engine no trigger_response reaches the player (walking into the first page on the cross stone sends none, with the interact object as a trigger or as a kinematic body), so without this no page could be collected on any input. The player gets the same paper messages the trigger sent.
